headline: NLW made the case for Google's Gemini 4 Neon, a model he says puts Google back in the race at the top of the table, while the headlines tallied the first trading day after Anthropic's record IPO.

themes.title: Gemini 4 Neon and model diversity
themes.body: NLW says Google released Gemini 4 Neon just before the Anthropic IPO, its fourth model in two months. Artificial Analysis scored it 61 on its Intelligence Index, one point behind GPT-6.2 Astra and four behind Fable 5.2. NLW argues Gemini does not need to be better to be useful: Neon reframed an episode outline where OpenAI and Anthropic models stayed in Wikipedia mode.

themes.title: Anthropic's first trading day
themes.body: NLW reports Anthropic closed its first NASDAQ day at $97.17, up 17 percent from its $83 IPO price, after raising $107 billion, the largest IPO in history, for a $1.8 trillion market cap. Bloomberg economist Anna Wong suggested the listing could mark the end of the AI trade, and Vanda Research's Viraj Patel said retail traded both sides with under $60 million net buying.

whyItMatters: With a third lab now close to the leaders on benchmarks, architects can treat model choice as a portfolio, using different models for the different perspectives they bring rather than standardizing on one vendor.

episodes.title: Why You Should Try Gemini Neon (Even if You Love Fable)
episodes.summary: Headlines cover the day after Anthropic's record $107 billion IPO, an AMD short report, Chinese reaction to new US chip export rules, and a White House cybersecurity personnel change. The main episode examines Google's Gemini 4 Neon, its benchmark results, and NLW's view that its different perspective is valuable despite it being a pushover. It closes with Apple's reported computer-use agent plans.
